source: NCERT Class IX, Democratic Politics I, Polity Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Learning from South Africa
points: **Apartheid** = the system of **racial discrimination** in South Africa, where the white minority oppressed the black majority.
**Nelson Mandela** (jailed 28 years) led the struggle; apartheid ended in **1994** with the first democratic election.
South Africa's new Constitution (praised worldwide) sought to **heal divisions and protect the rights of all** — showing how a constitution unites a divided society.

sections.heading: 2. Why a Constitution
points: A **Constitution** is the **supreme law** that: expresses **shared ideals**, defines how the **government is formed and its powers**, sets **limits on government**, and guarantees **citizens' rights**.
It generates a degree of **trust and coordination** among people.
It expresses the **aspirations** of a society.

sections.heading: 3. Making of the Indian Constitution
points: Framed by the **Constituent Assembly** (elected 1946); worked **1946–1949**; had **299 members**.
**Dr Rajendra Prasad** — President; **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** — Chairman of the **Drafting Committee**.
**Adopted 26 November 1949**; came into force **26 January 1950**.
It drew on the **freedom struggle**, the **Objectives Resolution (Nehru)**, and ideas from other countries.

sections.heading: 4. The Preamble and its Values
points: The **Preamble** states the guiding values: India is a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic**.
It secures for all citizens: **Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity**.
It begins with **"We, the People of India"** — the Constitution's authority comes **from the people**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Apartheid = racial discrimination (South Africa); Mandela; ended 1994.
Constituent Assembly (1946–49, 299 members); Rajendra Prasad = President; Ambedkar = Drafting Committee.
Adopted 26 Nov 1949; in force 26 Jan 1950.
Preamble: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic; Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
'We, the People of India' — power flows from the people.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ambedkar** headed the **Drafting Committee**; **Rajendra Prasad** was the Assembly's **President**.
Constitution **adopted 26 Nov 1949**, **enforced 26 Jan 1950**.
Preamble keywords: **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic** (Socialist & Secular added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).
**Apartheid** ended in South Africa in **1994** (Mandela).
